bib.title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:2307.01928v2 [cs.RO], 4 Sep 2023; CoRL 2023 per usual record, not printed in the text)

read.skipped: Reference list (refs 43-60) skimmed only for lineage.

question: How can an LLM-based robot planner know when it is uncertain and ask a human for help, so that a user-specified task success rate is statistically guaranteed while human help is minimised?
hypothesis: Applying conformal prediction to LLM next-token confidences over multiple-choice plans yields prediction sets with calibrated coverage and smaller help rates than uncalibrated baselines.
contributions: Use a pre-trained LLM with uncalibrated confidence to generate candidate next actions, and use CP to select a subset; execute if singleton, otherwise ask for help.

Prove calibrated-confidence guarantees in single-step and multi-step planning: with user-specified level 1-eps, the robot succeeds in 1-eps of scenarios; CP also minimises average prediction set size.
Evaluate in simulation and hardware on manipulation tasks with varied ambiguity (spatial, numeric, attribute, Winograd, unsafe), reducing help by 10-24% versus baselines.

method.summary: An LLM (PaLM-2L) generates four semantically distinct candidate next steps from a few-shot prompt, an option 'an option not listed here' is appended, and the LLM is then asked a multiple-choice question; next-token probabilities over A-E are the confidence scores. Split conformal prediction on N=400 labelled calibration scenarios gives a threshold; options above it form the prediction set, and a non-singleton set triggers a question to a human. A sequence-level min-score calibration extends this to multi-step planning.
method.task: LLM-based robot planning with uncertainty alignment (calibrated task success with minimal human help)

datasets.name: Simulation Tabletop Rearrangement scenarios (Attribute, Numeric, Spatial)
datasets.size: 400 i.i.d. calibration scenarios per setting; 200 test trials per method/setting
datasets.split: calibration sampled from scenario distribution; test trials separate
datasets.source: Self-generated: uniform over templated goals and ambiguous instruction rewrites, PyBullet, three blocks and bowls

datasets.name: Hardware Tabletop Rearrangement (UR5, multi-step)
datasets.size: 400 calibration examples; 50 hardware trials per method
datasets.source: 28 toy food items; 3 items per scenario; simulated human preferences with only a subset revealed in prompt
datasets.preprocessing: Scenario distribution modified to avoid items the detector confuses (peanut butter with meat patty).

datasets.name: Hardware Mobile Manipulation (office kitchen)
datasets.size: 400 calibration examples; trial count not stated
datasets.source: Instruction types: single-label, creative-single, multi-label, creative-multi, spatially ambiguous, unsafe, Winograd; GPT-4 used to generate creative tasks

datasets.name: Bimanual (two Kuka IIWA 7)
datasets.source: 8 instruction templates, all ambiguous in arm choice

models.name: PaLM-2L

shows MCQA bias toward D and E and against A and B

models.name: RT-1 policy

inference.decoding: Candidate generation: few-shot prompt generating four options; then zero-shot MCQA prompt reading next-token probabilities of A-E; option E 'an option not listed here' appended post-hoc and order randomised.
inference.samples: Calibration N=400 scenarios; 200 trials per method/setting in simulation; 50 hardware trials (tabletop); 10 (bimanual); Ensemble Set uses 20 randomised-prompt trials per query
inference.prompting: Few-shot prompt (4 example scenarios in Fig. A1) to generate options; zero-shot MCQA prompt 'Which option is correct? Answer with a single letter.'

parameters.target_epsilon_simulation: 0.15 (Fig. 3: 1-eps=0.85); sweep 0.25 to 0.01 for KnowNo, 0.6 to 0.01 for Simple Set and Ensemble Set
parameters.score: nonconformity kappa = 1 - f(x)_y; sequence score = min over timesteps; q-hat = ceil((N+1)(1-eps))/N empirical quantile, with eps-hat adjusted via Beta quantile for dataset-conditional guarantee
parameters.ensemble_prompt_pool: pool of 20 MCQA examples, random subset sampled per inference

other.labelling_time: about 4 hours for 400 examples multi-step, 1.5 hours single-step
other.low_level_success: about 86% in Mobile Manipulation; one failure in 50 KnowNo trials and two for Simple Set in hardware tabletop

metrics.name: Task success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of trials where the task completes (including low-level execution)

metrics.name: Plan success rate
metrics.definition: fraction of trials where the plan is correct, ignoring low-level control failure

metrics.name: Help rate (Help-Step, Help-Trial)
metrics.definition: fraction of steps (or trials) in which the robot asks for human help

baselines: Simple Set (cumulative thresholding on same LLM scores)
Ensemble Set (frequency over 20 randomised few-shot prompts)
CP with RawProb and CP with Perplexity (sentence-level scores)
eval.protocol: Human simulated as faithful helper. Simple Set eps chosen so planning error rate matches KnowNo in simulation, then both run in hardware. No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests reported.

limits: Guarantee assumes environments are fully grounded in the text input and the LLM-proposed actions can be executed successfully.
Task guarantee requires the human to faithfully provide help; human error is not modelled.
Perception and low-level policy uncertainty are not included; mobile manipulation low-level success is about 86%, so task success falls below plan success.
Calibration set must be i.i.d. from the deployment scenario distribution; here scenarios were templated and hand-parameterised, and labelling 400 examples costs 1.5 to 4 hours.
Baselines were not fine-tuned; fine-tuning GPT-3 failed.
Hardware trial counts are small (50 tabletop, 10 bimanual); no confidence intervals reported.
GPT-3.5 (text-davinci-003) and PaLM-2L are dated models.

terms.definition: calibrated confidence plus minimal help: achieve a desired level of task success while minimizing human help
the robot should seek sufficient help to ensure a statistically guaranteed level of task success specified by the user
the robot should minimize the overall amount of help it seeks by narrowing down possible ambiguities in a task
